Per-ICR Imprinting Deviations

Source: R/module_icr.R
AnalyzeICRStatus.Rd

Scores each imprinting control region (ICR) of a panel separately. For every sample and ICR with at least min_probes probes, the deviation is the median over the ICR's probes of beta - reference (median(beta) - 0.5 with the fixed reference). Each ICR has a single parental origin, so its deviation lies on one axis: a gain or loss of methylation on the paternal or maternal axis. Two-axis IDS/Angle for a single imprinted domain is obtained by scoring a locus panel such as chr11p15 or chr20q13 with AnalyzeImprintStatus().

Usage

AnalyzeICRStatus(
  betaFile,
  metaFile = NULL,
  probeset = "selected",
  genome = "hg38",
  dmr_type = NULL,
  reference = c("auto", "controls", "fixed"),
  reference_group = NULL,
  reference_samples = NULL,
  reference_beta = NULL,
  control_group = reference_group,
  control_samples = reference_samples,
  min_probes = 3L,
  delta_cutoff = 0.175,
  z_cutoff = 2
)

Arguments

betaFile

Data frame/matrix or file path containing probe-by-sample beta values, or an ImprintomeSet object.

metaFile

Metadata data frame or file path. Must be provided unless betaFile is an ImprintomeSet.

probeset

Character scalar naming a probeset key.

genome

Genome build of the probeset annotation, "hg19" or "hg38" (default "hg38"). Ignored when betaFile is an ImprintomeSet, whose own genome is used.

dmr_type

DMR_type values to score. NULL (default) scores every annotated ICR, gametic and secondary alike; the DMR_type column of the result records each ICR's type.

reference

How the balanced reference state is defined.

  • "auto" (default): use control samples when they are supplied, either external (reference_beta) or in-cohort (reference_group/ reference_samples). Fall back to the fixed 0.5 only when no controls are given, or when fewer than 3 are available (with a warning).

  • "controls": require a control reference; too few controls is an error.

  • "fixed": always use 0.5, the original behaviour.

With controls, each probe's reference is the median beta of that probe across the controls. Paternal and maternal deviations are medians of beta - reference, and IDS and Angle are computed from these deviations instead of from median - 0.5.

reference_group

Optional Sample_Group value(s) whose samples form an in-cohort control reference. Each control is itself scored against the other controls (leave-one-out).

reference_samples

Optional character vector of in-cohort control sample names, used instead of reference_group.

reference_beta

Optional external control reference, used when the cohort has no (or too few) controls. It can be one of:

  • a probe-by-sample beta matrix or data frame;

  • a beta file path;

  • a per-probe profile from BuildReferenceProfile(), given as the object or as an .rds path.

It should match the cohort's tissue, array type and preprocessing. Probes absent from the reference are dropped.

control_group, control_samples

In-cohort controls used to standardize deviations (z). Default to reference_group and reference_samples. Without controls, z is NA and calls use delta_cutoff only.

min_probes

Minimum number of probes for an ICR to be scored (default 3).

delta_cutoff

Minimum absolute deviation for an altered call (default 0.175).

z_cutoff

Minimum absolute z-score for an altered call when controls are available (default 2), or NULL for no z criterion.

Value

Data frame with one row per sample and ICR: sample metadata, probeset, ICR_name, ORIGIN, DMR_type, CHR, start, n_probes, median_beta, reference (median reference beta), deviation, abs_deviation, z, direction ("gain" or "loss") and altered. Settings are stored in attribute icr_settings.

Details

An ICR is called altered when abs(deviation) >= delta_cutoff and, if z_cutoff is set and control samples are available, also abs(z) >= z_cutoff. Both criteria are symmetric, so gains and losses are called alike. For sample i and ICR k, with deviation d[i, k],

z[i, k] = (d[i, k] - median(d[C, k])) / max(SD(d[C, k]), 0.02),

where C is the set of controls, excluding i when i is itself a control. The standard deviation is floored at 0.02 so that very homogeneous controls do not inflate z. When the controls also form the reference, each control's deviation is computed leave-one-out as well, so control z-scores are out-of-sample in the same way as those of cases. z is reported whenever at least 3 controls are available; with fewer than 10 a warning notes that the control median and SD are unstable.

The defaults (delta_cutoff = 0.175, z_cutoff = 2) were selected under the prespecified threshold-selection protocol in the package repository (benchmark/, amendment 5), by leave-one-cohort-out cross-validation on six development cohorts with leave-one-out control z-scores, and evaluated in three additional cohorts. Earlier versions used delta_cutoff = 0.075 with z_cutoff = 3 (control z-scores computed in-sample), and before that delta_cutoff = 0.15. The thresholds were selected with control samples (in-cohort, or external controls of the same tissue and platform), so that the z criterion applies. Without controls z is NA and only delta_cutoff is applied; that setting was not evaluated and calls are exploratory.

See also

SummarizeICRStatus() for the per-sample multi-locus summary and PlotICRHeatmap().
